newsitem.title: INDIA: India police name ex-PM Gandhi, others in gun deal - paper.
newsitem.headline: India police name ex-PM Gandhi, others in gun deal - paper.

text.p: India's federal police have named late prime minister Rajiv Gandhi as the main accused in a probe into a controversial $1.3 billion artillery contract, the Indian Express newspaper said on Wednesday.
The chargesheet also names other people, including a former minister and top bureaucrats, whom the Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) was seeking to prosecute, the daily said.

The proposed chargesheet had been sent to the government for formal clearance, the daily quoted sources in the cabinet as saying. Under Indian law, the CBI needs government sanction to proceed with prosecutions, even of former civil servants.
Once a chargesheet is formally approved the CBI can file a regular chargesheet in the courts.

The newspaper said the CBI report alleged that Gandhi, who was assassinated in 1991 while campaigning, was guilty of conspiring to cause willful loss to the state exchequer and of allowing middlemen to profit from the purchase of howitzers from Sweden's Bofors AB.
The CBI probe also said it failed to prove that Gandhi had benefited financially from the deal, the newspaper said.
Rajiv Gandhi had all along denied any involvement. His family has also denied any involvement in the 1986 guns deal, one of India's longest-running scandals.
CBI officials were not immediately available for comment.
Swiss police say there is evidence that Bofors paid about $40 million into various bank accounts in Switzerland during the time the contract with India was drawn up and settled.
The CBI has already named Italian businessman Ottavio Quattrocchi and his wife, Maria, as recipients of illegal payments made by Bofors.

Quattrocchi was the representative of Italian engineering firm Snamprogetti Spa in New Delhi when India signed the deal with Bofors. He now lives in Malaysia. He and Snamprogetti have denied any involvement in the alleged payments.
India has asked Malaysia to arrest and extradite Quattrocchi and his wife.
The CBI has also named businessman Win Chadha, the Indian agent for Bofors, and his wife and son as recipients of the payments. Chadha, who now lives in Dubai, has denied the allegations.
